posts.body_html:
Visited my home-slice Rob Co of THE PITCHER PLANT PROJECT last weekend (damn, was too shy to ask for an autograph), and chilled for a bit, talking the usual geek language that only fellow readers and ourselves can understand, haha! We discussed top secret crosses, and surmised how to produce them. Mad props for having me over Rob-dawg!

I had to snap a couple of pictures, as his collection is about 2 weeks ahead of my outdoor crop. It was surprising to see how some of the flavas were at about the same stage of development, whereas the alatas and hybrids were far ahead.

All photos were taken 3/14/14:






These seedlings can easily fill up this entire greenhouse when they get bigger. You have no idea how amazing some of these will become in the future-you could tell even some of the tiny seedlings stood out already:



S. flava 'heavy veined' is what this is called. It looks more like a S. flava "up-side-down cuprea":


Rob had to cover his nepenthes because they were recovering from frost damage (the greenhouse is unheated, and we had a cold snap a few months ago where it was down to 28F...Yes, I know, that's nothing compared to the polar vortex, but it's like alaska to us Californians ), although they're coming back quite well:



What's cookin' over here? A beautiful S. flava var. cuprea from Dean Cook, of course!


Overview shot with the table waking up. FINALLY! Every spring is always exciting:


Some very nice hybrids from Eric (great work btw Eric! Definitely some unique stuff up in there that has great potential):


The endangered S. oreophila section:



Some cool hybrid:



Adrian slack x Judith Hindle-a sibling to S.x Elaine Wang!



same clone, Face view:



And last but not least, same clone. Isn't that color just awesome?!
